title: The weak commutator and the variable-coefficient regularizer error
reviewed_arguments: All 33 original obligations, 25 displays, three complete solutions and the original diagram remain.
The full bounded weak form permits a Hermitian indefinite matrix principal part and every complex lower term on either form domain.
Explicit coefficient norm bounds, intrinsic derivatives, supported/restricted actions and common compact norm supports justify all maps.
Scalar componentwise localizers and their actual adjoints give legal antidual source pairings.
The real principal commutator has the correct minus-two-imaginary sign and every ordinary-normal coefficient term.
Only coefficient adjoints move in the commutator identity; the full complex lower form remains in the exact source equation.
The arbitrary-gap estimate uses the exact mean tester order, a right parametrix and the negative separated remainder.
Proper arbitrary-real-order realization and mixed localization supply L2 values for transformed positive-order coefficients.
Every lower-defect term has tester order s-1 = nu-3/2, including unequal-gap normal terms, without normal integration by parts.
The lower form on the output remains until an actual positive-factor comparison is available.
The full regularizer error expands all principal and lower coefficients and gives a uniform V-to-antidual bound at fixed supports.
The regularized equation retains its actual forcing commutator and does not assert an L2 strong realization.
Strong adjoint form convergence follows from symbol convergence and density; strong L2 convergence is proved on the full L2 space.
The antidual representing map is a linear onto isometry; its induced inner product and completeness justify orthogonal projection.
Dense L2 image in either form antidual includes weak Neumann boundary sources; the explicit approximation bound proves strong dual convergence.
The fixed-input commutator converges to the full cutoff commutator, which need not vanish. Higher-order microlocal bounds and shrinking-width limits are separate.
All three solutions, three finite model groups and the original identity/map diagram were checked; computations do not replace analytic proofs.
later_scope_not_claimed: Positive-symbol construction and its uniform norm estimate
RW4 and full analytic boundary propagation
Remaining corner, systems, crossings and complex-phase obligations
